title: Subtle Scheming Detection: Can Monitors Catch Plausibly-Deniable Misbehavior?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Testing monitors on the hardest, most realistic threat model (plausibly-deniable scheming) directly measures whether monitoring is viable against sophisticated agents. This is the core question for AI control's long-term viability.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating plausibly-deniable scenarios requires deep understanding of both the task domain and what makes sabotage subtle. The CoT extraction investigation adds complexity. Beginners would need heavy mentorship to design convincing scenarios.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 15 synthetic scenarios is substantial design work. Comparing against obvious sabotage and investigating CoT extraction are separate experiments. Could be narrowed to 5 scenarios and drop the CoT investigation to fit 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
